summary.name: Kompas
summary.one_liner: Kompas is an open-source (MIT) desktop app that gathers your reading, notes and AI conversations into a connected graph and helps you grow them into writing.
use_cases: turn reading highlights and voice notes into essays or drafts
connect new ideas to past notes and decisions
run AI brainstorming sessions grounded in your own notes
keep a record of founder decisions and the reasons behind them
run local AI models over private notes with Ollama
summary.what_it_does: Kompas captures documents, highlights, voice notes and web pages into one library, marked as yours. Sessions start from a topic, and the app pulls in past notes, decisions and reading to ask follow-up questions. Each session leaves linked traces (decisions, memories, retrieved passages) that form a graph, and a session can be moved into a draft where relevant past work appears. The page says Kompas writes with the user rather than for them. Free desktop data stays on the device; the only network calls go to the LLM providers the user chooses.
notable: Open source desktop app under MIT license
Bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic, Claude Code/Codex subscription, or local Ollama models
Local-first: sessions, notes and graph stay on device on Free
Pro tier adds cross-device sync and built-in hosted AI
caveats: Cross-device sync and built-in frontier AI require the paid Pro tiers
Realtime voice and audio transcription require an OpenAI key
No web app; browser is only used for sign-up, account and billing
Pro hosted cloud cannot be self-hosted
